title: Automated Architectural Blueprint Archiving
business: A global architectural firm managing thousands of high-resolution CAD files for active construction projects.
problem: The firm faces rising storage costs and administrative overhead from keeping all project versions in a single, high-performance storage tier, even after projects reach completion.
solution: Amazon S3 provides a durable object storage solution where files are organized into buckets. By applying lifecycle policies, the firm can automatically transition completed project files to lower-cost storage classes and enforce deletion after a mandatory retention period, while bucket policies ensure only authorized project leads access sensitive blueprints.
steps: Create a dedicated S3 bucket to serve as the central repository for all architectural blueprints.
Define an S3 bucket policy to restrict access to specific IAM roles associated with project leads.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle rule to transition objects to a colder storage class 90 days after project completion.
Set an expiration rule within the lifecycle configuration to permanently delete files after seven years of archival.
Enable S3 Versioning to maintain a history of changes for every blueprint uploaded to the bucket.
outcome: The firm achieves automated compliance with data retention requirements while significantly reducing storage costs by moving inactive blueprints to appropriate tiers without manual intervention.
limitation: A critical limitation is the eventual consistency model for certain operations and the potential for increased latency when retrieving objects from archived storage classes, which can be verified by monitoring the time-to-first-byte during retrieval requests.
